clauses.title: The map routes the writer's commit and push through the packaged operations
requires: | The bounded batch's one normal commit (CL-D89) | `commit_create` | `created` (data of `workspace_create`), `captured` (envelope of `operator_capture`), `message` |

| The bounded batch's one non-force push (CL-D89) | `push_publish` | `created` (data of `workspace_create`), `captured` (envelope of `operator_capture`), `parent` (the public head the batch built on: the captured head for the first batch, the run's last pushed head after; CL-D99) |

clauses.title: The capture records the operator identity and refuses a missing or unusable one
The commit carries the captured identity and the push names one helper without force
requires: HEAD does not descend from the captured public head

clauses.title: CL-D89 records the identity, the helper, and the superseded CL-D37 clause
clauses.section: ## CL-D89 — The writer commits and pushes through packaged operations with the operator identity
requires: *Owner choice:* Option A for the identity
naming a second credential helper, admitting an SSH or other non-https remote, adding force in any form, or letting anything but the writer invoke either operation requires a new owner decision.

clauses.title: The CL-D89 fixtures drive the capture, the commit, the push, and the boundary
requires: Issue #181 commit_create commits with exactly the captured identity under isolated config
Issue #181 push_publish never forces over a remote that moved

clauses.title: The structural boundary admits exactly the two operations, from publish.js only
